To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the prostaglandin synthesis was improved by immobilization of microsomes on CaSO4 containing silica gel.
the prostaglandin synthesis was improved by immobilizing the microsomes on Ca2+ containing silica gel.

immobilization of goat vesicular prostaglandin microsomes on CaSO4 containing silica gel G (silica gel-G) increased the yield of prostaglanding by 1.6 fold in comparison to the free microsomal enzyme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a simple and inexpensive method for the stabilization of the prostaglandin synthetic activity by immobilization of the enzyme on solid supports.
the immobilization of goat vesicular prostaglandin microsomal particles on solid supports and the stabilization of the immobilized prostaglandin enzyme.
the immobilization of prostaglanidn synthetase and stabilization of the enzyme activity by immobilization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
immobilization of microsomes on CaSO4-containing silica gel G is a very effective procedure for stabilization of prostaglandins synthetase activity.
immobilization of prostaglanding synthetase in a solid phase by adsorption of microsomal vesicles on silica gel G is a promising approach for the production of prostaglandins on an industrial scale.
the immobilized prostaglandin system has the following advantages over the free microsomal system: (a) increased yield, (b) stability, (c) reusability and (d) easy recovery of the products.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

prostaglandin synthesis by microsomes is a Ca2+-dependent enzymatic process and immobilization of microsomes by adsorption on a Ca2+-containing solid matrix like silica gel-G would stabilize prostaglandin formation.
immobilization of goat vesicular prostaglandin synthesizing system on silica gel-G containing CaSO4 is an effective method to stabilize the enzymatic activity.
the stabilization of prostaglandins synthetase by CaSO4 is the key to the immobilized microsome preparation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
immobilized prostaglandin synthesizing enzyme can be stabilized by the presence of divalent metal ions in the silica gel.
immobilization of prostaglanin synthetase is a viable approach to stabilize prostaglandin production.
immobilization of prostagalandin synthetase on silica gel G containing CaSO4 is the best way for the stabilization of the enzyme.
